analysis.title: GS Basics: Rates Calm. Cost of Capital. TTF new Highs
key_insights: Asia equity indices are flat, but there is heavy chop beneath the surface as AI-related concerns build. KOSPI was up 1-2% after falling 5.5% the day before, then turned slightly lower, as did Samsung and Hynix, after the first read on ASML.

ASML reported headline blowout numbers, raised the lower end of 2026 guidance and cited demand extending into 2029/30. The author says the company will not have enough capacity to meet customer demand. The sticking point is no upgrade to 2027 expectations, and the market wanted a more meaningful upward reset to next year's earnings.

Williams lowered the temperature on 2027 rate hikes. The author reads this as the Fed wanting to stay on hold in October unless forced to act. CPI on 14 Oct is the key test, with consensus at 0.6% headline and 0.2% core.

Bonds have been rallying, rate vol is compressing and some of the recent financial tightening is beginning to reverse. The author cites very one-sided positioning as a tailwind, and worries about the ex-AI economy (weak consumer confidence) as supportive for bonds.

Heating oil is threatening to retest its highs and is the energy price the author watches most closely. There is no real solution to the distillate shortage, and Russian diesel exports are unlikely to change the near-term picture.

European gas (TTF) took out its highs earlier in the week and stands at 86. The author calls this both an inflation problem and increasingly an economic problem as higher fuel costs filter through the system.

Google's Gemini 4 Argon is out and competing at the frontier. The author says Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta are all in contention and the frontier has never been this competitive. Anthropic holds a closed-door investor event on 14 Oct.

CCC credit spreads are around 1,250bp, over 200bp wider since September. BB and single-B spreads have widened much less. Part of the CCC move is idiosyncratic distress in legacy media, cable and building products, but HY has widened in aggregate.

Sovereign deficits and AI financing needs through 2028 create a very large demand for capital. The author is not convinced AI crowding-out drives CCC weakness. The broader question is whether the cost and availability of capital become prohibitive for lower-quality borrowers. A few AI-vertical names show notable CDS increases.

The author is fundamentally bullish on AI technology but sees the limiting factor as the ability to finance and deliver supply (financing, power, construction, equipment), not demand. Intermediaries between strong end demand and undeliverable supply risk an air pocket in orders, which the author suspects worries the semiconductor supply chain, possibly as a 2027 or 2028 event.

The author says winners are those who control scarce compute and capacity, and that hyperscalers are correctly seen as secular beneficiaries of the inference economy. Competition among labs may compress model economics without undermining infrastructure owners.

market_movers.rationale: Headline blowout numbers, raised lower end of 2026 guidance, and demand cited out to 2029/30 with capacity short of demand. The market wanted an upgrade to 2027 expectations, which did not come.

sector_views.rationale: Demand is strong, but the author flags a risk of an air pocket in orders for the semi supply chain, possibly in 2027 or 2028, if financing and physical bottlenecks limit spending.
They are seen as secular beneficiaries of the inference economy and own much of the scarce infrastructure.

earnings_insights: ASML reported headline blowout numbers (reported, per the author's first read), raised the lower end of its 2026 guidance, and cited demand extending into 2029/30. It gave no upgrade to 2027 expectations, which the author says the market wanted.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus for the print on 14 Oct. The author calls CPI the key litmus test for a Fed that wants to stay on hold.
Consensus for the print on 14 Oct.
TTF took out its highs earlier in the week. The author calls it an inflation problem and increasingly an economic problem.
More than 200bp wider since September. The author is watching for migration into single-B, leveraged loans and primary issuance.

risk_factors: Cost of capital and availability of financing for lower-quality borrowers and AI spending through 2028.
Physical bottlenecks (power, construction, equipment) could prevent demand from becoming spending, creating an air pocket in orders in the semi supply chain.
Broadening credit stress would extend beyond AI to SMEs, consumers and the wider economy.
Distillate shortage and higher heating oil and TTF gas prices feeding inflation and growth risk.
Escalation in the Saudi/Houthi conflict could lead to attacks on energy infrastructure.
vol_and_positioning: Rate vol is compressing as bonds rally.
The author describes positioning as very one-sided, a tailwind for bonds.
Some of the financial tightening of recent weeks is beginning to reverse.
geopolitical: Zelensky shows some willingness to engage, but there is little evidence the odds of a Russia/Ukraine resolution have materially improved.
Saudi escalation against the Houthis raises the risk of further retaliation against energy infrastructure. The latest attack hit Aramco corporate headquarters, not oil assets.
Russian diesel exports are unlikely to change the near-term distillate shortage.

tension_points.bear_case: Cost of capital and physical bottlenecks in financing, power, construction and equipment may stop demand from becoming spending, risking an air pocket in orders for the semi supply chain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broadening credit stress, such as migration of spread widening into single-B, leveraged loans and primary issuance, would signal that capital is becoming prohibitive.
